sections.label: Equity Market Development Programme funding
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates that the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme funding demonstrates genuine commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: In particular, I appreciate that the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP) funding demonstrates genuine commitment.

sections.label: SGX companies return on equity
sections.summary: As of end January 2026, 61% of SGX companies generated return on equity below 8%, compared to Japan and Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Putting aside the comparisons with other western developed markets, as of end January 2026, 61% of Singapore Exchange (SGX) companies generated return on equity below 8%, compared to 44% in Japan and 24% in Korea.

sections.label: SGX-listed companies trading volume
sections.summary: Only 14 SGX-listed companies have daily trading volume above US$20 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Only 14 SGX-listed companies have daily trading volume above US$20 million.

sections.label: Mandatory value-up disclosure requirements
sections.summary: The speaker says listed companies feel no compulsion to improve fundamentals and calls for mandatory value-up disclosure requirements immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: While we are asking the EQDP fund managers to deploy more than $5 billion in capital and expect returns, our listed companies feel no compulsion to demonstrate commitment to improving fundamentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: We must institute mandatory value-up disclosure requirements immediately.

sections.label: Directors and CEO remuneration disclosure
sections.summary: SGX rules require disclosure of directors and CEOs' remuneration since January 2023, yet only 68% of companies disclosed exact remuneration by December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: SGX rules require disclosure of directors and chief executive officers' remuneration since January 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Yet, only 68% of companies disclose exact remuneration by December 2024.

sections.label: Singapore stock market capitalisation
sections.summary: Singapore's stock market capitalisation as a share of national output stood at 117% last year, between India and Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore's stock market capitalisation, as a share of national output, stood at 117% last year, between India and Malaysia.

sections.label: Singapore venture capital market size
sections.summary: One estimate puts Singapore's venture capital market at about $1.2 billion in 2024, far below the Bay Area or United Kingdom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One estimate places our venture capital market at around $1.2 billion in 2024, a small fraction of the more than $4 billion raised by comparable early-stage rounds from either the Bay Area or the United Kingdom.

sections.label: Few IPOs and Catalist listings
sections.summary: There were six IPOs last year and four the year prior, with Indonesia and Malaysia dominating ASEAN listings and fundraising.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Last year, there were only six IPOs and it was four the year prior.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) bourses have all found greater success in their public offerings with Indonesia and Malaysia dominating the region in terms of listing as well as fundraising capacity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must shore up local listings on Catalist to increase its attractiveness as an exit destination for our otherwise robust earlier stage venture ecosystem.

sections.label: GEMS and IPO stimulus
sections.summary: Breaking SGX's negative equilibrium requires temporary IPO stimulus; GEMS underwrites listing expenses but favours main board listings over Catalist.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Breaking this negative equilibrium that SGX has found itself in will require, pardon the pun, a catalyst in the form of temporary stimulus to IPO activity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It has, since 2019, sought to underwrite listing expenses with the Grant for Equity Market Singapore Scheme (GEMS), but GEMS is presently biased in favour of main board listings rather than Catalist and it is unclear how much take-up there has been for this scheme.

sections.label: Family offices and stock liquidity
sections.summary: Enhancing stock market liquidity should also involve family offices, whose tax treatment under sections 13O and 13U requires minimum qualifying investments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Enhancing stock market liquidity should not be limited, of course, to public sector incentives alone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should also enlist our ecosystem of family offices more into this effort – the favourable tax treatment for family offices under sections 13O and 13U of the Income Tax Act only applies when a minimum allocation is made to qualifying investments.

sections.label: Domestic stock market goal
sections.summary: Only then will Singapore have a domestic stock market commensurate with its status as a global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Only then will we have a domestic stock market, commensurate with our status as a global financial centre and only then can we make Singapore equities great again.

sections.label: SGX average daily traded value
sections.summary: The average daily traded value of securities on SGX grew more than 20% year-on-year to almost $1.8 billion in November 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The average daily traded value of securities on SGX grew more than 20% year-on-year to almost $1.8 billion in November 2025.

sections.label: IPO activity rebound
sections.summary: IPO activity rebounded last year with over $2.4 billion raised, the highest since 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The IPO activity rebounded significantly last year, with more than $2.4 billion in total funds raised, which is the highest level since 2019.

sections.label: EQDP fund management allocation
sections.summary: $3.95 billion was allocated across nine asset managers under EQDP to develop fund management and investor participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For instance, we have allocated $3.95 billion across nine asset managers under EQDP to develop our fund management industry and to increase investor participation in our market.

sections.label: Building equities market capabilities
sections.summary: Singapore builds capabilities rather than forcing outcomes, aiming for an equities market focused on shareholder value creation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are also not trying to force outcomes through quotas or administrative allocation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are building capabilities – in fund management, in listed companies' ability to enhance shareholder value, to engage investors, we are investing in market infrastructure – so that investors and issuers choose Singapore because they are convinced that this makes commercial sense and this has longer-term strategic value for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our goal is to build an equities market where companies sharpen their attention on shareholder value creation, communicate their strategies clearly, optimise capital allocation and thus deliver good shareholder returns.

sections.label: Multi-year equities market effort
sections.summary: A multi-year, partnership-based effort aims to grow Singapore's equities market in depth, resilience and attractiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: So, the two are not mutually exclusive, they go hand-in-hand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We also want an equities market where research coverage is broader and more insightful, where market makers operate with clarity and confidence and where trading and post‑trade are efficient and user‑friendly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is how our market will earn capital and participation in a sustainable way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is a multi‑year effort that requires discipline, willingness to innovate sensibly and committed partnership among Government, regulators, exchanges, intermediaries, investors and listed companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have laid the foundations and set in motion a comprehensive programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If we keep at this work together in close partnership between Government and industry, and with the right incentives and a clear focus on quality and sustainability, I am confident that Singapore's equities market will grow in depth, resilience and attractiveness in the years ahead.
